summary: Instagram is carrying the channel: most videos get 1,200-1,400 views there, while YouTube Shorts mostly gets under 100 views. The best videos are the ones with a surprising, funny or 'robot fails' angle (gyro robot falling, clap switch, PIR sensor), and they also get the most likes and saves. Plain 'How does X work?' videos on everyday objects (taps, doors, smoke alarms, touchscreen) get far fewer views, and the one English video earned almost nothing on Instagram.
winningPattern: Hindi videos about a robot or maker-project sensor (gyro, clap switch, PIR, IR, line follower, mic) with a bold, surprising claim as the hook, like 'X can't do Y, it only does Z' or 'without X the robot falls'. Titles are short Hinglish with one emoji and #shorts, and the video shows a robot or Arduino module in action. Posted on Instagram first, where it gets ~1,200+ views; YouTube only picks up the ones with a strong curiosity hook (gyro, clap switch, PIR).
doMore: Make robot and Arduino-module videos showing something failing or surprising, such as 'without sensor X the robot does Y'.
Use 'it doesn't do A, it only does B' contrast hooks like the Clap Switch and Mic titles.
Keep the 3-5 day cadence of maker-project topics that earned 1,200+ IG views, and repeat what works within 2 days.
Ask viewers to save the video ('save this for your project') since saves are high on the build-focused videos.
Test each winning topic on YouTube with a punchier first-second visual, because YouTube is far weaker than IG for the same content.
stopDoing: Generic everyday-object explainers (mall door, washroom tap, lift, street light) that average under 500 IG views.
Posting several near-duplicate topics (two smoke detector, two IR sensor, two automatic tap videos) in the same week.
English-language videos for now, since the audience responds to Hindi.
